prompt: A Python CLI tool called pwcheck that evaluates password strength. Command: pwcheck <password> prints a score 0-4 and a verdict (very weak/weak/fair/strong/very strong). Scoring: +1 each for length >= 8, length >= 12, mixed upper+lowercase, at least one digit, at least one special character, capped at 4. A --json flag emits {score, verdict, suggestions} where suggestions names each missing criterion. Empty password exits with code 1 and an error on stderr. Scoring logic must live in a module separate from the CLI. Include unit tests for every scoring rule and the suggestion list, plus one integration test invoking the CLI via subprocess.

A TypeScript library called slugkit exposing two functions: slugify(input, options?) converting arbitrary text to a URL-safe slug (lowercase, spaces and punctuation to single hyphens, no leading/trailing hyphens, unicode letters transliterated to ASCII where trivial or dropped otherwise, maxLength option truncating at a hyphen boundary) and deslugify(slug) converting a slug back to space-separated words. Strict TypeScript, no dependencies. Include jest unit tests covering: punctuation collapse, hyphen trimming, maxLength boundary behavior, empty input returning an empty string, and a deslugify round-trip.

A Rust CLI tool called quickstats that reads newline-separated numbers from a file and prints count, mean, median, min, max, and standard deviation, each on its own labelled line with values rounded to 4 decimal places. A --json flag prints the same fields as one JSON object. Non-numeric lines are skipped with a warning to stderr; an empty or missing file exits with code 1 and a message on stderr. The statistics functions must live in a library module separate from main.rs. Include unit tests for each statistic including the even/odd median cases, plus an integration test running the built binary on a fixture file.
